properties.project_name: Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks -- emergency stabilization and planned demolition
properties.digitized_from: No Assessor block/lot exists for this Port tideland/water-lot facility (confirmed: DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' Socrata dataset, acdm-wktn, has no PIER-numbered street_name entries at all near this site, consistent with pier and dry-dock structures sitting outside the Assessor's secured roll). No Port GIS shapefile or site-plan figure for the Piers 68/70 shipyard footprint was available to digitize from directly, so this is a coarse locational box only, centered near the shipyard's known entrance at 20th and Illinois St (a real intersection in DataSF's official street centerlines) and sized to sit between the tracked Pier 70 parcel's own northern edge (Crane Cove Park, max latitude 37.76406) and Mission Bay South's nearest tracked features (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage and the P24 waterfront lawn, both of which reach south to roughly latitude 37.7644-37.7648) -- the real Piers 68/70 shipyard, described in Port materials as a 13-acre facility at the 'northeast corner' of the complex including Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock, occupies this narrow shoreline gap and extends east into the Bay itself, which this box does not attempt to trace. CORRECTED 2026-10-10: the outline is now two hand-traced hull outlines -- Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock -- on Esri World Imagery (zoom 20, imagery captured 2025-08-29 per docs/satellite-imagery.md). The earlier placeholder box lay in open water north of the shipyard. Hulls were told apart by length: the Port Commission memo (Calendar Item 9A, 2026-01-09) and Mission Local (2026-02) give Dry Dock No. 2 as a 900 ft (274 m) floating dock built in 1970 and the Eureka as 528 ft (161 m), built in 1945; the large eastern hull measures about 283 m and the central hull about 169 m including wing walls. No source read says which hull sits where, so this match is Pier & Point's own inference. Still no Assessor parcel, Port GIS layer or site-plan figure to trace from.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- two hand-traced hull outlines from satellite imagery, accurate to a few metres at best, not a surveyed footprint and not a Port or Assessor geometry. Which hull is Dry Dock No. 2 and which is the Eureka is inferred from their measured lengths against the lengths the Port memo and Mission Local give; no source read places them. The outlines cover the two floating hulls only, not the 13-acre shipyard: the Pier 68 wharf arms, the quay, the cranes, the sheds and four unidentified floating tank sections west of the Eureka are left out. Needs replacement with a real digitized footprint if a Port GIS layer or the Dry Dock Memorandum's own site figure becomes available.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Port tideland/water-lot facility; not on the Assessor's secured roll (data.sf.gov acdm-wktn has no PIER-numbered parcels near this site).
properties.regulatory_context: Dry Dock No. 2 (a ~1940s-era floating dry dock) developed excessive listing after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding in November 2025; the Port Commission President and Executive Director declared an emergency on 2025-12-08 (Port Commission memo, Calendar Item 9A, 2026-01-09). Port staff anticipate advertising a demolition-services contract in summer 2026 for Dry Dock No. 2 and the neighboring Eureka Dry Dock (a second floating dry dock at Piers 68/70, formerly USS Steadfast/AFDM-14 -- not the 1890 ferryboat Eureka at Hyde Street Pier/SF Maritime NHP). Total estimated cost of stabilization and disposal is $61.2M (Capital Planning Committee memo, 2026-02-09); see the record file for the funding breakdown and what remains unfunded.
properties.notes: Distinct from and outside the boundary of Brookfield's tracked 28-acre Pier 70 D4D redevelopment parcel and the separately-delivered Crane Cove Park, per the Port's own description of the Pier 70 shipyard/dry docks as a separate 13-acre facility (closed 2017) at the complex's northeast corner.
properties.digitization_method: 2026-09-28 -- CREATED as a coarse locational box (see accuracy_caveat and digitized_from), not a traced footprint: no Assessor parcel, Port GIS layer or site-plan figure was available. Anchored between the tracked Pier 70 parcel's real northern edge (Crane Cove Park) and Mission Bay South's nearest tracked features, near the shipyard's documented 20th/Illinois St entrance, then shifted east (further into the Bay, consistent with piers/dry docks projecting past the shoreline) so it does not overlap Crane Cove Park's or the UCSF Illinois Street Garage's real, already-tracked footprints (check_geometry_quality.py --strict). No owner review yet; replace with a real digitized footprint if a Port GIS layer or figure becomes available. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. digitized_from reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- digitized_from: 'No Assessor block/lot exists for this Port tideland/water-lot facility (confirmed: DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' Socrata dataset, acdm-wktn, has no PIER-numbered street_name entries at all near this site, consistent with pier and dry-dock structures sitting outside the Assessor's secured roll). No Port GIS shapefile or site-plan figure for the Piers 68/70 shipyard footprint was available to digitize from directly, so this is a coarse locational box only, centered near the shipyard's known entrance at 20th and Illinois St (real DataSF street-centerline intersection, data/raw/official_street_centerlines.geojson) and sized to sit between the tracked Pier 70 parcel's own northern edge (Crane Cove Park, data/manual/pier70_crane_cove_park.geojson, max latitude 37.76406) and Mission Bay South's nearest tracked features (the UCSF Illinois Street Garage and the P24 waterfront lawn, data/processed/approximate_projects.geojson, both of which reach south to roughly latitude 37.7644-37.7648) -- the real Piers 68/70 shipyard, described in Port materials as a 13-acre facility at the 'northeast corner' of the complex including Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock, occupies this narrow shoreline gap and extends east into the Bay itself, which this box does not attempt to trace.'. 2026-10-10 -- CORRECTED: the 2026-09-28 box (lon -122.3859 to -122.3847, lat 37.7644 to 37.7660) lay in open water north of the shipyard, found on Esri World Imagery (zoom 20, captured 2025-08-29). Replaced with a two-part shape tracing the two floating dry-dock hulls: Dry Dock No. 2 as an 8-corner outline (the narrower bow at its north end is kept, hence not a plain rectangle) and the Eureka as a rectangle. Reviewed with the owner: Dry Dock No. 2 accepted as first drawn; the Eureka was first rotated 2 deg counter-clockwise about its centre, which overhung the hull, so it was re-fitted to the hull's edges at 1.8 deg, then rotated a further 1.7 deg (about 3.5 deg in all) at the owner's request. geometry_type stays approximate.
